microtheory.name: cortical_microcircuit
microtheory.definition: The canonical 6-layer cortical microcircuit — the building block repeated across all cortex. Specific cell types, layer-specific connectivity, intrinsic dynamics. Douglas + Martin's canonical circuit (1991, 2004) defines the recurrent template. Understanding this circuit at this level means understanding how cortex computes — the same fixed architecture handles vision, audition, language, planning. Substrate analogue: a Mt is the substrate's repeated computational unit; its internal structure is what this Mt describes.

concepts.name: pyramidal_neuron
concepts.definition: The cortex's primary excitatory output. Triangular soma, long apical dendrite reaching to L1, basal dendrites near soma. ~80% of cortical neurons. Substrate analogue: a Mt's exporting concept.

concepts.name: basket_cell
concepts.definition: Fast-spiking parvalbumin-positive inhibitory interneuron. Synapses on the soma of pyramidal neurons; controls firing rate. Substrate analogue: temperature regulation of a Mt's overall activation.

concepts.name: chandelier_cell
concepts.definition: PV+ interneuron synapsing on the axon initial segment of pyramidal neurons. Most powerful inhibition — can veto a pyramidal cell entirely. Substrate analogue: hard veto on individual concept firing.

concepts.name: martinotti_cell
concepts.definition: SST+ (somatostatin) interneuron. Inhibits the apical dendrites of pyramidal cells, gating top-down feedback. Substrate analogue: gates feedback influence on each concept.

concepts.name: vip_interneuron
concepts.definition: Vasoactive intestinal peptide interneuron. Disinhibits — targets SST cells. Activated by neuromodulators; opens up the cortex during attention. Substrate analogue: arousal-modulated gain on cortical processing.

concepts.name: spiny_stellate_cell
concepts.definition: L4 excitatory interneuron in sensory cortex. Primary recipient of thalamic input. Substrate analogue: input concept receiving from world adapter.

concepts.name: layer_1
concepts.definition: Mostly axons + dendrites from below. Few cells (Cajal-Retzius). Receives long-range cortico-cortical + thalamic feedback. Apical tufts of pyramidal cells synapse here. Substrate analogue: top-down feedback collection layer.

concepts.name: layer_2_3
concepts.definition: Cortico-cortical pyramidal neurons. Send long-range horizontal connections to other cortical areas; receive feedback from L1. Bulk of local recurrent computation. Substrate analogue: cross-Mt communication concepts.

concepts.name: layer_4
concepts.definition: Granular input layer. Receives thalamic input (in sensory cortex). Spiny stellates. Primary input gate. Substrate analogue: input-receiving concept layer.

concepts.name: layer_5
concepts.definition: Large pyramidal neurons projecting to subcortex (brainstem, thalamus, basal ganglia, cord). Cortical output. Substrate analogue: output concepts to world adapter.

concepts.name: layer_6
concepts.definition: Pyramidal cells projecting back to thalamus + local cortex. Feedback to input. Substrate analogue: backward edges modulating input gating.

concepts.name: canonical_microcircuit
concepts.definition: Douglas + Martin 1991. The repeating cortical circuit template: thalamus → L4 → L2/3 → L5 (output) + L6 (feedback to thalamus). Same architecture in every cortical area; specialisation comes from inputs + plasticity, not circuit changes. Substrate analogue: every Mt has the same structural template — input concepts, processing concepts, output concepts, feedback edges.

concepts.name: cortico_cortical_loop
concepts.definition: Two cortical areas connect both feedforward (L2/3 of lower → L4 of higher) AND feedback (L5/6 of higher → L1 of lower). Bidirectional information flow. Substrate analogue: bidirectional genlMt connections.

concepts.name: lateral_inhibition
concepts.definition: Within a cortical column, active pyramidal cells inhibit nearby pyramidal cells via interneurons. Sharpens selectivity; implements winner-take-all. Substrate analogue: substrate's argmax over Concept space within a Mt.

concepts.name: feedforward_inhibition
concepts.definition: Input that excites pyramidal cells also excites interneurons, which then inhibit the same pyramidal cells with a delay. Limits how long the cell can fire from a single input — sets a temporal window. Substrate analogue: bounded-duration firing of any concept per input.

concepts.name: recurrent_excitation
concepts.definition: Pyramidal cells in L2/3 + L5 are heavily connected to each other within a column. Recurrent excitation drives persistent activity + attractor dynamics. Substrate analogue: the substrate's CAN within-Mt couplings.

concepts.name: balance_of_excitation_inhibition
concepts.definition: Each cortical neuron receives roughly equal excitation + inhibition. Operates near the balance point — slight tip determines output. Critical for fluctuation-driven coding + criticality. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ near 0 = high-entropy decision point.

concepts.name: asynchronous_irregular_state
concepts.definition: Healthy cortex's default state. Each neuron fires irregularly + asynchronously with neighbours; population firing is steady but unsynchronised. Mean-field theory predicts this. Substrate analogue: substrate's idle Mt state — distributed activity without synchronisation.

concepts.name: neural_avalanche
concepts.definition: Brief synchronous bursts cascading through cortex. Size distribution follows a power law — signature of self-organized criticality. Substrate analogue: substrate's cascading event flux across connected Mts.

concepts.name: ne_glia_interaction
concepts.definition: Astrocytes wrap around synapses (tripartite synapse). Modulate neurotransmitter clearance; release gliotransmitters; calcium-wave signalling. Substrate analogue: substrate's normalisation + temperature regulation distributed across Mt edges.

concepts.name: microglia
concepts.definition: Brain's resident immune cells + active synapse pruners during development. Substrate analogue: the prune_Mt correction's mechanism — selecting which connections to remove.

concepts.name: oligodendrocyte
concepts.definition: Produces myelin in CNS. One oligodendrocyte myelinates ~50 axon segments. Substrate analogue: consolidation mechanism that speeds up frequently-used paths.

rules.name: every_cortex_uses_same_microcircuit
rules.head: any cortical area handling any computation
rules.body: uses the same canonical microcircuit template — Douglas+Martin 1991. Specialisation comes from inputs + plasticity, not architectural changes. Substrate analogue: every Mt uses the same template; specialisation is from its concepts + edges.

rules.name: L4_receives_L23_processes_L5_outputs
rules.head: input arrives at a cortical microcircuit
rules.body: L4 receives it; L2/3 processes it via recurrent dynamics; L5 outputs to subcortex; L6 sends feedback to input. Substrate analogue: Mt's input-process-output-feedback shape.

rules.name: inhibition_carves_selectivity
rules.head: an excitatory input could activate many candidate responses
rules.body: interneuron-mediated lateral inhibition sharpens selectivity by suppressing all but the strongest. Substrate analogue: argmax-via-inhibition within Mt's concept space.

rules.name: balance_keeps_cortex_at_criticality
rules.head: cortical excitation is balanced with inhibition
rules.body: the network operates near the critical point — neither silent nor seizing. Maximum information transmission. Substrate analogue: substrate's tuning of temperature β keeps it at the productive edge of state space.

rules.name: glia_modulate_substrate_dynamics
rules.head: synapses are active over time
rules.body: glial cells (astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes) modulate them on slow timescales — clearing, pruning, myelinating. Substrate analogue: long-timescale Mt restructuring via correction + consolidation handlers.
